messages:
ops-bot: [ALERT] High rate of 504 gateway timeouts from services in us-west-2b to internet destinations. Metric: ELB/504 > baseline by 18x.

 aisha: getting pages from external monitors too. A subset of app hosts in us-west-2b can't reach downstream SaaS vendor endpoints. Anyone on network oncall? :phone:

 oncall-net: grabbing it. pulling VPC flow logs, route tables, and any recent infra runs. assigning to rafael for triage.

 rafael: first pass: several subnets in us-west-2b show 0 egress TCP responses. flow logs show SYNs leaving, then DROPs. Checking NAT config now.

 priyanka: FYI I saw an automated cleanup job run ~11m ago in the infra account. It was meant to delete stale resources older than 30d. Could that have removed a NAT?

 rafael: describe-route-tables shows route 0.0.0.0/0 pointing at nat-0f1e2d3c for rtb-0bcd1111 which used to be a healthy NAT in us-west-2b. But describe-nat-gateways shows nat-0f1e2d3c state = deleted.

 zack: how did we end up with a deleted NAT referenced in a route? usually deleting a NAT doesn't auto-remove the route target. If some automation removed NAT while RT association still pointed at it, that would blackhole.

 rafael: checking CloudTrail: at 17:04:22 UTC, an internal lambda "cleanup-orphaned-nat" executed DeleteNatGateway(nat-0f1e2d3c). It logged success. The route wasn't touched. The lambda had a bug that matched tags too aggressively.

 incident-bot: Incident created INC-177346 (sev: high)  Owner: oncall-net.

 aisha: customer impact? I have two paying customers reporting increased error rates for embedding upload jobs. Can we give a quick mitigation ETA?

 priyanka: mitigation options ranked by speed:
 - Recreate NAT gateway (fast-ish but AWS mentions pending ENI creation and it can take 5-10m plus quota checks)
 - Launch an HA NAT instance in the same AZ and update the routes to point to the instance's ENI (manual but instant once booted)
 - Re-associate subnets to a route table that points to a healthy NAT in another AZ (works but may hit cross-AZ bandwidth/cost and existing elastic IP limits).

 rafael: I'm going to attempt a quick NAT re-create first (aws ec2 create-nat-gateway) while priyanka stands up a NAT instance as a hot fallback.

 priyanka: building a tiny nat instance AMI from our golden image, user-data includes iptables MASQUERADE. Spinning up t3a.medium in us-west-2b and attaching an Elastic IP.

 aisha: customers need a status line. customer-success-bot, can you push a brief update?

 customer-success-bot: Notifying impacted customers list (C-120, C-421, C-599). Draft: "We are investigating partial egress failures for services in us-west-2b; mitigation underway. No data loss expected. We will provide updates every 15 minutes."

 rafael: create-nat-gateway returned NAT ID nat-0a9b8c7d in pending. CloudWatch NATGateway ErrorCount still high for previous id but new NAT not yet available.

 priyanka: nat instance is up, EIP allocated. Configured ip-forwarding and iptables. Trying route update now. Command: ```aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-0bcd1111 --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --instance-id i-0abc1234 --region us-west-2```

 zack: careful - replace-route with instance target means that the route uses instance as gateway only for legacy EC2-Classic; for VPC we need to set target to network-interface. Use --network-interface-id eni-0fff2222 or use instance route through attachment?

 priyanka: good catch. updating to use the instance's primary ENI: ```aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-0bcd1111 --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --network-interface-id eni-0fff2222 --region us-west-2```  executed.

 rafael: performing connectivity tests from an app host in affected subnet: curl to https://api.thirdparty.com returned 200. Latency slightly higher but traffic flows.

 aisha: awesome. keep the route change for now while NAT gateway creation completes. We should also block further runs of cleanup lambda.

 priyanka: toggling lambda to paused state and revoking its IAM DeleteNatGateway permission in a staging test. Patching CI job to require preflight confirmation.

 incident-bot: Reminder: follow-up update due in 15 minutes for INC-177346.

 rafael: new NAT gateway nat-0a9b8c7d created and in available state. It has allocation id eipalloc-0c1d2e3f attached. Replacing routes to point back to the native NAT gateway now for long-term. Command: ```aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-0bcd1111 --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --nat-gateway-id nat-0a9b8c7d --region us-west-2```

 zack: after switching back to managed NAT, we should terminate the NAT instance and release EIP to avoid cost. But hold for a few minutes to confirm traffic stable.

 aisha: logs show retry spikes for model-fetch jobs between 17:02 and 17:12 UTC. Ticketing customers for potential delayed jobs. Also escalated to billing if retries cause overages.

 priyanka: deleting the temporary nat instance now (i-0abc1234) and releasing the EIP. Verified route points to nat-0a9b8c7d and test traffic ok.

 rafael: root cause summary for now: automated cleanup lambda incorrectly matched tag pattern and deleted an in-use NAT gateway. Route tables pointed to now-deleted NAT, resulting in blackholed egress for those subnets.

 aisha: handoff: my shift ends in 20m. rafael, can you be incident owner for the next 40 minutes and then hand to zack? Make sure artifacts (CloudTrail, flow logs, lambda activity) are uploaded.

 rafael: will take ownership. uploading logs to INC-177346 artifact store and noting exact CLI commands in incident notes.

 priyanka: postmortem action items (brief): fix cleanup lambda matching logic; add a dry-run check + approval for resource deletions; prevent DeleteNatGateway in production without 2nd approval; add runbook step to prefer route failover to healthy NATs when NAT gateway is DELETING/DELETED.

 customer-success-bot: Customer update posted: "Mitigation applied via temporary NAT instance and new managed NAT; services should be functioning. We will follow up with postmortem."

 rafael: next update in 30m or on any regressions. thanks team for fast coordination. :thumbsup:
